title: Neki van – Expressing “To Have” in Hungarian

sections.heading: How Hungarian expresses “to have”
paragraphs: Hungarian does not have a direct verb meaning “to have.”
Instead, possession is expressed using the structure 'neki van' (to him/her there is) along with a possessive noun ending.

sections.heading: Affirmative Examples
list: Nekem van autóm – I have a car
Neked van könyved – You have a book
Neki van macskája – He/She has a cat
Nekünk van házunk – We have a house
Nektek van tollatok – You all have a pen
Nekik van kertjük – They have a garden

sections.heading: Negative Examples
list: Nekem nincs autóm – I don’t have a car
Neked nincs könyved – You don’t have a book
Neki nincs macskája – He/She doesn’t have a cat
Nekünk nincs házunk – We don’t have a house
Nektek nincs tollatok – You all don’t have a pen
Nekik nincs kertjük – They don’t have a garden

sections.heading: Question Examples
list: Van autód? – Do you have a car?
Van könyve? – Does he/she have a book?
Van macskájuk? – Do they have a cat?
